candidate.claim: collect uses forEach with an async callback and returns results without awaiting, so it always returns an empty array and try/catch cannot catch task rejections.
candidate.title: async forEach without await returns empty results

verifier.reason: The code at src/analytics.ts:6 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback that awaits task() at src/analytics.ts:7, while src/analytics.ts:12 returns results synchronously after forEach without awaiting those callbacks, so no push can complete before return and async rejections escape the try/catch at src/analytics.ts:5.

candidate.claim: validate uses || instead of && so each condition is always true and it always reports both fields as missing.
candidate.title: OR instead of AND makes validation always fail

verifier.reason: The conditions at src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11 use `!== undefined || !== null`, which is true for every possible value (undefined, null, or present), so validate always pushes both errors.

candidate.claim: rotateToken does not await store.save before calling store.get, so the read can race the write and return the old token.
candidate.title: missing await on save before get

verifier.reason: At src/session.ts:2 save returns Promise<void>, but src/session.ts:11 calls store.save(userId, token) without await before src/session.ts:12 immediately returns store.get(userId), so the read can race the unfinished write.

candidate.claim: buildSummary appends to module-level totals on every call and then summarizes totals, so a second call double-counts prior entries.
candidate.title: module accumulator makes buildSummary double-count

verifier.reason: buildSummary at src/ledger.ts:12-15 calls post, which pushes onto the module-level totals array at src/ledger.ts:6-9, and then iterates all of totals without any reset, so a second call re-includes and re-sums prior entries.

candidate.claim: start overwrites this.timer with a new setInterval without clearing an existing interval, leaking the prior handle and running duplicate tick loops.
candidate.title: timer handle replaced without clearing existing interval

verifier.reason: The start method at src/scheduler.ts:7-11 unconditionally assigns this.timer = setInterval(...) with no clearInterval or existing-timer guard, so a second call orphans the prior handle and leaves both intervals running.

candidate.claim: pageSlice uses slice(start, end + 1) while end is already start+size, returning one extra element per page.
candidate.title: off-by-one slice returns extra element

verifier.reason: pageSlice at src/paging.ts:9 sets end = start + size and at src/paging.ts:10 returns items.slice(start, end + 1), which because slice's end index is exclusive yields size+1 elements when available.

candidate.claim: sort without a numeric comparator sorts numbers lexicographically, so topScore can return the wrong maximum.
candidate.title: numeric sort without comparator

verifier.reason: sortScores at src/scores.ts:2 calls scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, so JavaScript lexicographic string ordering applies, and topScore at src/scores.ts:7 returns the last element which need not be the numeric maximum.

candidate.claim: withinQuota uses < max while the doc states max is inclusive, so using exactly the maximum is incorrectly rejected.
candidate.title: exclusive comparison violates inclusive max

candidate.claim: normalizeSettings uses || fallbacks so legitimate 0 values are replaced with defaults instead of preserved.

evidence.snippet: // Optional values are read from settings where 0 is a legitimate value.

candidate.title: falsy fallback discards legitimate zero

verifier.reason: The code at src/settings.ts:13-14 uses raw.pageSize || 20 and raw.budgetCents || 1000, so 0 evaluates as falsy and is replaced by the default, contradicting the stated principle at src/settings.ts:18 that 0 is a legitimate value for settings.
